## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery and one-click launch mechanics

## Description

Delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated, browsable set of
getting-started tutorials that a user can launch into their own project with
one click. Notebook tutorials open a workbench in the user's project with the
tutorial notebook loaded; pipeline tutorials import the pipeline into the
user's project. The gallery reads tutorial packages conforming to the tutorial
packaging format (package metadata and pinned images), so tutorial content can
be updated and versioned without Dashboard releases. This addresses the
blank-platform problem: today the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms.

## Scope

- A tutorial gallery section in the Dashboard (navigation entry, tutorial
  listing, and tutorial detail view) backed by tutorial packages conforming to
  the tutorial packaging format.
- One-click launch mechanics:
  - Notebook tutorials: open a workbench in the user's project with the
    tutorial notebook loaded, using the pinned image the package specifies.
  - Pipeline tutorials: import the pipeline into the user's project.
- Gallery surfaced where new users land in the Dashboard so the curated set is
  discoverable at first login (time-to-first-success is the strategy's driver).
- Ability to enable/disable the gallery through Dashboard configuration,
  consistent with existing per-component feature flags administered via
  `OdhDashboardConfig`.
- Incidental UI copy and help-text updates that fall out of the gallery change
  (no new documentation content — that is authored separately).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user with a project, when they open the tutorial gallery, the
  curated tutorial set is listed with its package metadata (title, journey,
  tutorial type).
- Given a notebook tutorial package conforming to the tutorial packaging
  format, when the user launches it from the gallery, a workbench opens in
  their project with the tutorial notebook loaded and the package's pinned
  image selected.
- Given a pipeline tutorial package conforming to the tutorial packaging
  format, when the user launches it from the gallery, the pipeline is imported
  into the user's project.
- Launch flows are verified against tutorial packages that conform to the
  packaging format (including the curated set once it is available).
- The gallery can be enabled and disabled through Dashboard configuration
  without a code change.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: "The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook,
  or importing the pipeline)." — Fully covered by this epic: the gallery UI and
  both launch flows. Also provides the launchability that the curated tutorial
  set depends on.

# Tutorial packaging format and validation harness

## Description

Defines the tutorial packaging format that makes tutorials versioned and
testable independently of Dashboard releases, and delivers the validation
harness that executes a package's validation manifest. A tutorial package
carries metadata describing the tutorial, references to pinned images, and a
validation manifest; the harness runs that manifest so any tutorial can be
tested against a target release on demand, without coupling tutorial releases
to Dashboard releases.

## Scope

- Format specification for tutorial packages:
  - Package metadata describing the tutorial (title, core journey, tutorial
    type — notebook or pipeline, entry point).
  - Pinned image references (the platform-maintained workbench images the
    tutorial runs on).
  - A validation manifest describing how the tutorial is tested.
- Versioning rules that let tutorial packages be published and updated
  independently of Dashboard releases.
- A validation harness that executes a package's validation manifest against a
  target release and reports pass/fail.
- A reference (sample) package that demonstrates the format end to end.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format defines package metadata, pinned-image references, and
  a validation manifest for tutorial packages.
- A tutorial package can be versioned and published without requiring a
  Dashboard release.
- The validation harness executes a package's validation manifest and produces
  a pass/fail result, demonstrated with the reference package against a target
  release.
- Packages can pin the platform-maintained workbench images so tutorial runs
  are reproducible.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: "A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases." — Fully covered by this epic. The
  strategy labels the HLR P1, but the epic's priority is promoted to P0 by
  priority inheritance: the Dashboard gallery consumes the format and the
  curated tutorials are packaged and validated per it, so it enables all P0
  work in this strategy (promotion recorded as a health warning in the
  decomposition summary).

# Six curated getting-started tutorials

## Description

Authors the six curated tutorials covering the platform's core journeys —
first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first
deployment, first RAG app — as tutorial packages conforming to the tutorial
packaging format, each tested against the current release through its
validation manifest. Notebook tutorials run in workbenches; the pipeline
tutorial is a pipeline definition the user imports into their project.

## Scope

- Six tutorials covering the named core journeys:
  1. First workbench
  2. Data prep
  3. First training run
  4. First pipeline
  5. First deployment
  6. First RAG app
- Each tutorial packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest) and versioned as a package.
- Consistent curation across the set: shared structure, difficulty ramp, and
  cross-references between journeys.
- Validation of each tutorial against the current release via its validation
  manifest, covering the platform surfaces the tutorials exercise:
  - Workbench (notebook) tutorials run in a workbench launched with the
    package's pinned image (Notebooks surface).
  - The pipeline tutorial imports and runs through the Data Science Pipelines
    surfaces (KFP v2 import).
- RHOAI Pipelines involvement as reviewers for the pipeline tutorial content
  (the Data Science Pipelines component itself needs no code changes for this
  strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Six tutorials exist covering: first workbench, data prep, first training
  run, first pipeline, first deployment, and first RAG app.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata,
  pinned images, validation manifest).
- Each tutorial passes its validation manifest tests against the current
  release.
- Notebook tutorials run successfully in a workbench launched with the pinned
  image; the pipeline tutorial imports and runs successfully in a project.
- The set is consistently curated: shared structure and style across all six
  tutorials.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: "Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys:
  first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first
  deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release." —
  Fully covered by this epic, including the tested-against-current-release
  requirement via the packaging format's validation manifest. The passive
  components the tutorials exercise (Notebooks workbenches, Data Science
  Pipelines import) are validated through this epic's acceptance criteria.

# Tutorial gallery usage and contribution documentation

## Description

Documents the tutorial gallery for users and would-be contributors: how to
browse and launch tutorials into a project, and how to contribute new
tutorials (authoring, packaging, validation, and versioning). Per the
strategy's out-of-scope statement, no submission tooling ships this release —
the contribution process is documented only.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **Using the tutorial gallery** (user topic):
  - Browsing the curated tutorial set and its metadata.
  - Launching a notebook tutorial (workbench opens with the notebook loaded).
  - Launching a pipeline tutorial (pipeline import).
- **Contributing new tutorials** (contributor topic):
  - Authoring guidelines and the curation bar (structure, style, difficulty
    ramp of the existing set).
  - Packaging a tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
    images).
  - Running the validation manifest and testing against a target release.
  - Versioning tutorial packages independently of Dashboard releases.
  - The intake path available this release (manual; no submission tooling).
- Screenshots and captions of the gallery and launch flows as built.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A published documentation topic covers using the tutorial gallery:
  browsing, launching notebook tutorials, and launching pipeline tutorials.
- A published documentation topic covers the contribution process for new
  tutorials: authoring guidelines, packaging per the tutorial packaging
  format, validation, and versioning.
- The documentation accurately reflects the implemented gallery behavior and
  the packaged tutorial set, verified through technical review by the teams
  that built the gallery, format, and tutorials.
- Contribution documentation states clearly that submission tooling is not
  available this release and describes the manual intake path.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: "Documentation covers using the gallery and the
  contribution process for new tutorials." — Fully covered by this epic. Epic
  priority is P1 per the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy
  frontmatter priority `Major` → P1), not the HLR's P2 label.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019: Curated getting-started tutorial gallery

## Strategy Overview

The strategy delivers a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: maintained,
tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users launch into their own
project with one click. The problem statement itself identifies three
architecturally distinct work streams with different owners and review
processes: product code (gallery and launch mechanics), authored content (the
tutorials), and documentation. No open questions, no external dependencies,
no Staff Engineer Input section.

## Step 0 Triage Record

Triage evaluated and **not triggered**. The strategy is not S-sized
single-component single-team work: it spans multiple components (Dashboard,
Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines, Documentation) and, per the strategy's own
problem statement, multiple distinct work streams — code implementation,
substantive content authoring (six new tutorials), and documentation. The
multiple-work-streams escape condition applies; full decomposition follows.

## Component Classification

| Component | Classification | Handling |
|-----------|----------------|----------|
| Dashboard | Active (code changes: gallery UI + launch mechanics) | Implementation epic E001 |
| Notebooks | Passive (no notebook-controller changes indicated; tutorials run on workbenches) | Validation ACs on E001 (workbench opens with notebook, pinned image) and E003 (notebook tutorials run in workbenches) |
| Data Science Pipelines | Passive (pipeline tutorials import via existing KFP v2 surfaces) | Validation AC on E003 (pipeline tutorial imports and runs) |
| Documentation | Docs content work | `docs-authoring` epic E004 |

**Component mapping notes** (canonical names from `.context/rhai-components.txt`):

- E002 (packaging format) and E003 (tutorials) both map to canonical
  `Notebooks`: the tutorials are primarily notebooks launched into workbenches,
  and the format's pinned images are the platform-maintained workbench images
  (see `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/notebooks.md`).
- E003's work spans `Data Science Pipelines` (the first-pipeline tutorial is a
  pipeline definition imported via KFP v2); the span is recorded here and the
  DSP-side validation is an acceptance criterion on E003 rather than a separate
  epic — the strategy frames the tutorials as one curated, tested set.
- E002's format is consumed by the Dashboard gallery (E001's code parses the
  package metadata); this cross-component consumption is captured by the
  E002 → E001 DAG edge, not by combining component names.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Component | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|-----------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E001 | Dashboard tutorial gallery and one-click launch mechanics | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E002 | Tutorial packaging format and validation harness | Implementation | Workbenches | Notebooks | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E003 | Six curated getting-started tutorials | Implementation | Workbenches | Notebooks | P0 |

E004's priority is P1 per the `docs-authoring` priority exception: the

    E002 --> E003["E003 Six curated tutorials"]

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements; no HLR is co-located with

## Health Warnings

- **Priority inversion (HLR-3 / E002)**: the strategy labels the tutorial
  packaging format P1, but both P0 HLRs build on it — the gallery code parses
  the format (Rule 13 edge) and the tutorials are packaged and validated per
  it (Rule 12 edge). By priority inheritance, E002 is promoted to P0 (an epic
  blocking all P0 work is implicitly P0). Flagged for human verification: if
  the product intent is that the gallery and tutorials can ship first against
  an interim ad-hoc packaging and the formal format lands later, decouple
  E002 from E001/E003 and restore its P1 priority; as written, the strategy's
  P0 "tested against the current release" requirement depends on the format's
  validation manifest, so the promotion is faithful to the stated scope.
- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then Acceptance Criteria section, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements. Team assignments are inferred from
  `.context/architecture-context/` owning teams (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard,
  Notebooks → Workbenches); the documentation team is inferred as RHOAI
  Documentation. Epic acceptance criteria are derived from the HLRs. If the
  actual team model differs (e.g., the pipeline tutorial is owned/validated by
  RHOAI Pipelines rather than reviewed by them), reassign before scheduling.
- **Passive-component assumption**: Notebooks and Data Science Pipelines are
  classified passive — the strategy attributes all launch mechanics to the
  Dashboard, and `notebooks.md` confirms the Dashboard owns the spawn UI. If
  loading a notebook into a freshly spawned workbench turns out to require
  notebook-controller changes (rather than an image/startup mechanism the
  Dashboard drives), a notebook-controller epic would need to be added; the
  mechanism choice is an implementation detail for the Dashboard team, and the
  outcome is pinned by E001's acceptance criteria.
- **Planning note (epic size)**: the six curated tutorials epic (E003) is
  above the ~2-week guideline by scope arithmetic — six authored, packaged,
  and validated tutorials at roughly two to three days each. Kept as one
  logical change: the six form a single curated set with shared style,
